relevance_note: Case report of an identifiable man with Danon disease and his affected mother: "We describe a case of a 30-year-old man with Danon's disease"; no LAMP2 variant is printed.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; small JSON built with a scratch Python script from hand-chosen values and checked span by span. Two in-scope people: the case-report patient (label 'patient') and his mother ('mother of patient'), both stated to have Danon's disease diagnosed by muscle biopsy and immunohistochemical LAMP-2 protein deficiency. No genetic testing or LAMP2 variant is reported, so the variants table is empty (the paper does not tie a variant to either person; diagnosis is by protein deficiency). Year from the abstract citation '(PACE 2008; 31:125-128)'. Age 30 recorded as age at last evaluation/time of report (it is the age at admission; follow-up ran to about 8+ months later). Vital status left not reported (follow-up described but alive not stated). The paper text is broken by a page break between 'aspartate' (line 36) and 'transaminase and alanine aminotransferase were increased.' (line 44); CK and AST/ALT elevation are therefore supported by two separate spans, not joined. Preexcitation nuance: the ECG showed a 'WolffParkinson-White (WPW) pattern' / 'preexcitation-like aspect' with short PR, but the authors state '2:1 AV block excluded WPW syndrome' and that preexcitation is probably due to HCM or enhanced AV nodal conduction; recorded pre-excitation pattern observed and WPW syndrome excluded as separate features (not treated as a contradiction). Skeletal myopathy checklist item marked observed for both from the biopsy statement about 'both cases' (mother: inferred from group statement; patient also has 'mild muscle weakness'). 'Mental retardation', 'ophthalmic abnormalities' and sudden death in the abstract/Discussion are general disease descriptions, not attributed to these people, and were not recorded. Device malfunction (T-wave oversensing) not recorded as a phenotype; high ventricular pacing threshold recorded as the authors attribute it to the storage disease.
